question: Should OpenClaw expose outbound delivery failures to agents as a shared system event, a structured message-tool/agent delivery status, or both?
rationale: The choice changes model-visible context, channel ownership, plugin SDK expectations, and recovery semantics, so source inspection can show the gap but cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Shared Typed Contract
options.body: Define a single delivery-failure/status contract over existing durable outbound outcomes and decide exactly where agents can observe it.

options.title: Tool Status Only
options.body: Return structured failure status to message-tool and agent-deliver callers without injecting new system events into sessions.

options.title: Keep Narrow Paths
options.body: Treat the current CLI, pending-final, cron, and channel-specific notices as sufficient and close this feature as not planned later.

recommendation.title: Shared Typed Contract
recommendation.body: Define a single delivery-failure/status contract over existing durable outbound outcomes and decide exactly where agents can observe it.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history trail for the shared outbound, channel delivery, and agent runtime seams points to this owner.
